easy.question: What does the verse command us to do with everything we have been commanded?
answers: Keep and observe it
Choose only the easy parts
Tell it to others
easy.explanation: The verse commands: “You shall keep all these words and do them”—that is, preserve and carry out the entire commandment.

easy.question: What two things must not be done to the commandment?
answers: Remember and study it
Add to it or take away from it
Ask and answer questions
easy.explanation: The verse concludes: “You shall not add to it, nor take away from it.”

easy.question: What does the phrase “all these words” indicate?
answers: Only some of the words
Only new instructions
Everything that was commanded
easy.explanation: The word “all” shows that the command applies to everything that was said.

medium.question: Why does the verse forbid both adding to and taking away from the commandment?
answers: So that everyone can choose a different law
So that the commandment is kept exactly as given
So that it may sometimes be changed
medium.explanation: Together, these two prohibitions teach that the commandment must not be changed in either direction.

medium.question: In the phrase “nor take away from it,” what does “take away” mean?
answers: Add to it
Remember it
Reduce or remove part of it
medium.explanation: In this context, “take away” means to reduce or remove part of the commandment.

medium.question: What is the main order of instructions in the verse?
answers: Keep and do it, without adding or taking away
Add, take away, and then keep it
Take away, do it, and then add
medium.explanation: First the verse says to keep and do the entire commandment; afterward it forbids adding to or taking away from it.

challenge.question: What follows from the prohibition against adding to the commandment?
answers: A small change is permitted
Even a change intended to improve it is not permitted
It may be replaced with another custom
challenge.explanation: The prohibition against adding teaches that the commandment must not be changed, even with good intentions or a desire to improve it.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “all these words” emphasize together with the command to keep them?
answers: The entire commandment must be observed, not only selected parts
Only the easy commandments need to be observed
The commandment need not be practiced
challenge.explanation: The phrase “all these words” emphasizes that keeping and doing applies to the whole commandment.

challenge.question: What common principle is expressed by “do not add” and “do not take away”?
answers: The commandment should change from place to place
Details should be added to make it easier
The boundaries of the commandment must be preserved without changing it
challenge.explanation: The parallel prohibitions express one principle: the commandment must not be changed in either direction.

questions.question: What follows from the prohibition against adding to the commandment?
answers: A small change is permitted
Even a change intended to improve it is not permitted
It may be replaced with another custom
questions.explanation: The prohibition against adding teaches that the commandment must not be changed, even with good intentions or a desire to improve it.

questions.question: What does the phrase “all these words” emphasize together with the command to keep them?
answers: The entire commandment must be observed, not only selected parts
Only the easy commandments need to be observed
The commandment need not be practiced
questions.explanation: The phrase “all these words” emphasizes that keeping and doing applies to the whole commandment.

questions.question: What common principle is expressed by “do not add” and “do not take away”?
answers: The commandment should change from place to place
Details should be added to make it easier
The boundaries of the commandment must be preserved without changing it
questions.explanation: The parallel prohibitions express one principle: the commandment must not be changed in either direction.

paragraphs.title: Testing the prophet and faithfulness to the LORD

easy.question: Who might give the people a sign or wonder?
answers: A prophet or dreamer of dreams
A king or judge
A priest or Levite
easy.explanation: The verse says: “If there arise among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and gives you a sign or a wonder.”

easy.question: What does the Torah command if the prophet calls the people to worship other gods?
answers: Ask him for another sign
Do not listen to him
Worship the other gods
easy.explanation: The Torah commands: “You shall not hearken unto the words of that prophet.”

easy.question: Whom are the Israelites commanded to follow and obey?
answers: The prophet
The other gods
The LORD their God
easy.explanation: The passage commands them to follow the LORD, keep His commandments, and serve Him.

medium.question: Why must the people not listen to the prophet even if his sign or wonder comes true?
answers: Because no prophet should ever be believed
Because the LORD is testing whether they love Him and remain faithful
Because signs and wonders cannot happen
medium.explanation: The verse explains that the LORD tests the people to know whether they love Him with all their heart and soul.

medium.question: In the phrase “a sign or a wonder,” what is a “wonder”?
answers: A miraculous act or special sign
A law or commandment
A song or prayer
medium.explanation: The word appears alongside “sign,” so it refers to an extraordinary sign or miraculous act meant to influence the listeners.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in the passage?
answers: The people punish the prophet, and then he gives a sign
The prophet gives a sign, it comes true, and then he urges worship of other gods
The people worship other gods, and then the prophet is sent to them
medium.explanation: First the prophet or dreamer gives a sign; then it comes true; afterward he tries to persuade the people to worship other gods.

challenge.question: What can we conclude from the fact that the prophet is punished even though his sign comes true?
answers: Faithfulness to the LORD is more important than an impressive sign or miracle
Every sign is a lie
The people do not need to keep the commandments
challenge.explanation: The passage teaches that a miraculous sign is not enough; the message must lead to faithfulness to the LORD and His commandments.

challenge.question: Why does the passage mention that the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt and redeemed them from slavery?
answers: To explain where the sign occurred
To remind Israel of the LORD’s kindness and their obligation to Him
To teach that the prophet had been in Egypt
challenge.explanation: Mentioning the Exodus emphasizes that the LORD redeemed Israel, so they must not follow a tempter to other gods.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “to thrust you out of the way” mean in context?
answers: To lead you along a different physical road
To turn you away from the path and commandments the LORD gave
To send you back to Egypt
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes an attempt to turn someone away from faith and obedience to the LORD, not merely to change the direction of travel.

questions.question: What can we conclude from the fact that the prophet is punished even though his sign comes true?
answers: Faithfulness to the LORD is more important than an impressive sign or miracle
Every sign is a lie
The people do not need to keep the commandments
questions.explanation: The passage teaches that a miraculous sign is not enough; the message must lead to faithfulness to the LORD and His commandments.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt and redeemed them from slavery?
answers: To explain where the sign occurred
To remind Israel of the LORD’s kindness and their obligation to Him
To teach that the prophet had been in Egypt
questions.explanation: Mentioning the Exodus emphasizes that the LORD redeemed Israel, so they must not follow a tempter to other gods.

questions.question: What does the phrase “to thrust you out of the way” mean in context?
answers: To lead you along a different physical road
To turn you away from the path and commandments the LORD gave
To send you back to Egypt
questions.explanation: The phrase describes an attempt to turn someone away from faith and obedience to the LORD, not merely to change the direction of travel.

paragraphs.title: Standing firm against a close tempter

easy.question: Who might tempt a person to worship other gods?
answers: A relative or close friend
Only a foreign king
Only a stranger
easy.explanation: The passage mentions a brother, son, daughter, wife, or close friend.

easy.question: What does the tempter urge the person to do?
answers: Leave the land
Go and worship other gods
Fight other nations
easy.explanation: The tempter says: “Let us go and serve other gods.”

easy.question: What will happen after all Israel hears about the punishment?
answers: Everyone will leave the land
Everyone will worship other gods
They will fear and not repeat this evil act
easy.explanation: The verse says that all Israel will hear and fear, and will not again do such an evil thing.

medium.question: What does “your eye shall not pity him” mean in context?
answers: Do not show him pity
Do not look at him
Do not speak to him
medium.explanation: The phrase appears with “you shall not spare” and “you shall not conceal him,” so it means not to pity the tempter.

medium.question: What sequence of actions is described in the passage?
answers: All the people punish the tempter, and afterward the person exposes him
The tempter urges worship of other gods, the person does not listen, and the tempter is punished
The person worships other gods, and then the tempter warns him
medium.explanation: First comes the enticement, then the command not to listen, and finally the description of the punishment.

medium.question: Why does the Torah command that the tempter not be hidden?
answers: So that everyone will know who he is
So that he can escape
So that he can receive an important position
medium.explanation: Because the tempter seeks to turn people away from the LORD, he must not be concealed; the punishment is meant to deter the people.

challenge.question: What does the command that the accuser’s hand be first against the tempter teach?
answers: The accuser must lead all Israel
The tempter is punished only if the accuser is stronger
The person affected by the enticement must be first to carry out the judgment
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes: “Your hand shall be first upon him,” followed by the hand of all the people.

challenge.question: What is the significance of mentioning gods “near you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other”?
answers: The prohibition applies only to nearby nations’ gods
The prohibition applies to all foreign gods, near and far
It is permissible to worship distant gods
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions both nearby and very distant gods to emphasize that no foreign god may be worshiped.

challenge.question: Why does the passage mention the Exodus when describing the seriousness of the tempter’s sin?
answers: To remind Israel that the LORD freed them from slavery, so they must not leave Him
To explain how to travel to Egypt
To teach that Egypt was the only place of idolatry
challenge.explanation: The Exodus is presented as the LORD’s act of rescue, making the attempt to abandon His worship an act of ingratitude and covenant betrayal.

questions.question: What does the command that the accuser’s hand be first against the tempter teach?
answers: The accuser must lead all Israel
The tempter is punished only if the accuser is stronger
The person affected by the enticement must be first to carry out the judgment
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes: “Your hand shall be first upon him,” followed by the hand of all the people.

questions.question: What is the significance of mentioning gods “near you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other”?
answers: The prohibition applies only to nearby nations’ gods
The prohibition applies to all foreign gods, near and far
It is permissible to worship distant gods
questions.explanation: The passage mentions both nearby and very distant gods to emphasize that no foreign god may be worshiped.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the Exodus when describing the seriousness of the tempter’s sin?
answers: To remind Israel that the LORD freed them from slavery, so they must not leave Him
To explain how to travel to Egypt
To teach that Egypt was the only place of idolatry
questions.explanation: The Exodus is presented as the LORD’s act of rescue, making the attempt to abandon His worship an act of ingratitude and covenant betrayal.

paragraphs.title: Investigating a city suspected of enticement

easy.question: What did the people hear that certain men were urging the city to do?
answers: Worship other gods
Leave the city
Build a new city
easy.explanation: The men said: “Let us go and serve other gods.”

easy.question: Who enticed the inhabitants of the city?
answers: The priests
Worthless men
The elders
easy.explanation: The verse says that “certain men, the children of Belial,” went out and led the inhabitants astray.

easy.question: What does the Torah command when such a report is heard?
answers: Punish immediately
Leave the city
Inquire, investigate, and question carefully
easy.explanation: The matter must first be examined carefully before a final decision is made.

medium.question: What should be done after a report that people are urging worship of other gods?
answers: Investigate carefully whether it really happened
Believe every rumor immediately
Ignore the report
medium.explanation: The verse commands the people to inquire, investigate, and question carefully in order to establish the truth.

medium.question: Why does the Torah command an investigation before deciding what to do?
answers: To find another city
To make sure the report is true
To discover who built the city
medium.explanation: Only after the matter is proven true can it be determined that the abomination was actually committed.

medium.question: In the phrase “question carefully,” what does “carefully” mean?
answers: Secretly
Briefly
Thoroughly and precisely
medium.explanation: The series of commands to inquire, investigate, and question shows that the matter must be examined thoroughly and precisely.

challenge.question: In the tempters’ statement, what does “which you have not known” refer to?
answers: The other gods
The inhabitants of the city
The men who left the city
challenge.explanation: The tempters propose worshiping other gods and describe them as gods the listeners have not known.

challenge.question: What does the repetition of “inquire, investigate, and question” emphasize?
answers: That the investigation should be quick
That the inquiry must be thorough and use several approaches
That people must not be questioned
challenge.explanation: The many verbs emphasize that one rumor is not enough; the facts must be established through a careful investigation.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “among you” in the passage?
answers: The event happened in a distant city
The event happened outside the land
The problem was found within the community itself
challenge.explanation: “Among you” means within the city or community, so this is an internal problem rather than only an outside threat.

questions.question: In the tempters’ statement, what does “which you have not known” refer to?
answers: The other gods
The inhabitants of the city
The men who left the city
questions.explanation: The tempters propose worshiping other gods and describe them as gods the listeners have not known.

questions.question: What does the repetition of “inquire, investigate, and question” emphasize?
answers: That the investigation should be quick
That the inquiry must be thorough and use several approaches
That people must not be questioned
questions.explanation: The many verbs emphasize that one rumor is not enough; the facts must be established through a careful investigation.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “among you” in the passage?
answers: The event happened in a distant city
The event happened outside the land
The problem was found within the community itself
questions.explanation: “Among you” means within the city or community, so this is an internal problem rather than only an outside threat.

paragraphs.title: Destroying the sinful city and avoiding its spoil

easy.question: What are the people commanded to do to the city and everything in it?
answers: Destroy and burn them
Rebuild them
Move them to another city
easy.explanation: The passage commands that the city and everything in it be destroyed and burned with fire.

easy.question: What will happen to the city after it is burned?
answers: It will become a larger city
It will remain a permanent ruin and never be rebuilt
It will become a dwelling place
easy.explanation: The city will become a permanent heap, meaning it will never be rebuilt.

easy.question: What must not cling to a person’s hand from the devoted things?
answers: Anything at all
Only the animals
Only the city’s tools
easy.explanation: The verse says: “Nothing of the devoted thing shall cling to your hand.”

medium.question: What is done with the city’s spoil before the city is burned?
answers: It is divided among the residents
It is gathered into the middle of its street
It is hidden outside the city
medium.explanation: All the spoil is first gathered into the street, and then it is burned together with the city.

medium.question: In the phrase “nothing of the devoted thing,” what does “devoted thing” mean?
answers: Property intended for personal use
Something given as a gift
Something designated for destruction and forbidden to take
medium.explanation: Here, the devoted thing is everything designated for destruction and dedication to the LORD, so nothing may be taken from it.

medium.question: According to the passage, what may happen if nothing is taken from the devoted things?
answers: The LORD will turn from His anger and show mercy to the people
The city will be rebuilt
The spoil will be divided among the residents
medium.explanation: The verse connects refusing to take anything with the LORD turning from His anger, showing compassion, and multiplying the people.

challenge.question: Why is the spoil burned, rather than only the city?
answers: To keep the spoil in one place
To make rebuilding the city easier
So that none of it remains for private use
challenge.explanation: Burning the spoil makes clear that it is part of what was devoted to destruction and that no one may benefit from it.

challenge.question: What is the connection between “nothing shall cling to your hand” and the blessing at the end?
answers: Avoiding the devoted things is presented as a condition for the LORD to turn from His anger and grant mercy and blessing
Taking the spoil brings wealth and blessing
The blessing comes only after the city is rebuilt
challenge.explanation: The verse presents a condition and result: if nothing from the devoted things is taken, the LORD will turn from His anger, show mercy, and multiply the people.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the prohibition applies not only to property but to the entire city?
answers: The city will become a permanent heap
The spoil will be gathered into the street
The animals, along with the inhabitants, will be killed by the sword
challenge.explanation: The command explicitly includes the animals, showing that the destruction encompasses the inhabitants, property, and livestock.

questions.question: Why is the spoil burned, rather than only the city?
answers: To keep the spoil in one place
To make rebuilding the city easier
So that none of it remains for private use
questions.explanation: Burning the spoil makes clear that it is part of what was devoted to destruction and that no one may benefit from it.

questions.question: What is the connection between “nothing shall cling to your hand” and the blessing at the end?
answers: Avoiding the devoted things is presented as a condition for the LORD to turn from His anger and grant mercy and blessing
Taking the spoil brings wealth and blessing
The blessing comes only after the city is rebuilt
questions.explanation: The verse presents a condition and result: if nothing from the devoted things is taken, the LORD will turn from His anger, show mercy, and multiply the people.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the prohibition applies not only to property but to the entire city?
answers: The city will become a permanent heap
The spoil will be gathered into the street
The animals, along with the inhabitants, will be killed by the sword
questions.explanation: The command explicitly includes the animals, showing that the destruction encompasses the inhabitants, property, and livestock.

paragraphs.title: Conclusion: Doing what is right in the LORD’s sight

easy.question: Whose voice does the verse command the people to obey?
answers: The LORD your God
The king
The prophet
easy.explanation: The verse says: “When you shall hearken to the voice of the LORD your God.”

easy.question: What must a person keep?
answers: The customs of his ancestors
All the LORD’s commandments
The king’s words
easy.explanation: The verse commands the people to keep “all His commandments.”

easy.question: What must a person do in the sight of the LORD?
answers: Go to war
Build an altar
Do what is right
easy.explanation: The verse concludes: “To do that which is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.”

medium.question: According to the verse, what is required in order to do what is right in the LORD’s sight?
answers: Listening to the LORD and keeping His commandments
Being wealthy and respected
Learning the customs of the nations
medium.explanation: The verse connects listening to the LORD and keeping His commandments with doing what is right.

medium.question: In the phrase “which I command you this day,” who is speaking?
answers: You
I
They
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates that the speaker is giving the command to the listener that day.

medium.question: What is the main sequence of actions in the verse?
answers: Do what is right, listen, and then keep the commandments
Keep the commandments, do what is right, and then listen
Listen, keep the commandments, and then do what is right
medium.explanation: The verse presents listening to the LORD first, then keeping His commandments, and finally doing what is right.

challenge.question: What does “in the eyes of the LORD” teach about what is right?
answers: The determining standard is the LORD’s will
What is right is determined only by human opinion
What is right depends on wealth
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that an action must be right according to the LORD’s will, not merely according to human judgment.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the word “all” in “keep all His commandments”?
answers: Keeping one commandment is enough
All the commandments must be kept
Only the priests must keep the commandments
challenge.explanation: The word “all” emphasizes complete observance rather than choosing only some commandments.

challenge.question: To whom is the command addressed in “which I command you this day”?
answers: To one person who is not an Israelite
To the leaders of the nations
To the listener, in the singular
challenge.explanation: The command is addressed directly to the individual listener.

questions.question: What does “in the eyes of the LORD” teach about what is right?
answers: The determining standard is the LORD’s will
What is right is determined only by human opinion
What is right depends on wealth
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that an action must be right according to the LORD’s will, not merely according to human judgment.

questions.question: What is emphasized by the word “all” in “keep all His commandments”?
answers: Keeping one commandment is enough
All the commandments must be kept
Only the priests must keep the commandments
questions.explanation: The word “all” emphasizes complete observance rather than choosing only some commandments.

questions.question: To whom is the command addressed in “which I command you this day”?
answers: To one person who is not an Israelite
To the leaders of the nations
To the listener, in the singular
questions.explanation: The command is addressed directly to the individual listener.
